chiefComplaint: One lower leg has become hot, swollen, red, and tender over two days.

historyAnswers.Onset and duration: Progression has been rapid over 36 hours.
historyAnswers.Itch versus pain: Warm and tender; pain is not out of proportion.
historyAnswers.New medications: No new medication in the past two months.
historyAnswers.Sun exposure and tanning: Outdoor exposure is intermittent; no tanning bed use.
historyAnswers.Personal and family skin cancer history: No personal skin cancer; family history reviewed.
historyAnswers.Pregnancy and contraception status: Pregnancy possibility and goals should be reviewed before teratogenic therapies.
historyAnswers.Systemic symptoms: Check vital signs, perfusion, and for fluctuance or signs of deeper infection.
historyAnswers.Focused clue: The redness expanded over two days after a small skin break; ask about diabetes, edema, prior episodes, and MRSA risk.

examFindings.General appearance: Alert and well appearing; record vital signs and assess severity in real practice.
examFindings.Focused lesion exam: Warm, tender, expanding erythematous plaque with edema on the lower leg; no fluctuance, bullae, necrosis, or pain out of proportion.
examFindings.Full skin exam: Inspect for a portal of entry, toe-web maceration, ulcers, and other sites of infection.
examFindings.Lymph nodes: Mildly tender regional nodes may be present; assess for lymphangitis.
examFindings.Nails and hair: No additional abnormality found on this maneuver.

image.alt: Independent teaching photograph, not the fictional patient’s record: A broad, confluent area of bright erythema and edema over the lower leg with an advancing margin; no obvious abscess in the supplied image.

tests.name: CBC and CMP
tests.result: Mild leukocytosis; renal function reviewed before antibiotic selection and dosing.

tests.name: Ultrasound
tests.result: No drainable collection identified if imaging is obtained because an abscess is uncertain.

tests.name: Bacterial culture
tests.result: No drainage is available to culture in this nonpurulent presentation.

tests.name: Photo documentation
tests.result: Baseline border and extent recorded for reassessment.

acceptableTreatments.name: Oral antibiotic
acceptableTreatments.reason: Choose an appropriate oral regimen using local guidance, allergy history, and severity; reassess if worsening.

unacceptableTreatments.name: High-potency topical corticosteroid on face or folds
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Site-related atrophy risk; choose site-appropriate treatment.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Systemic corticosteroid for an undifferentiated rash
unacceptableTreatments.reason: May obscure diagnosis and worsen some infections.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Methotrexate without baseline assessment
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Requires screening, labs, pregnancy precautions, and specialist oversight.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Biologic therapy without infection screening
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Requires appropriate screening and specialist plan.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Spironolactone without pregnancy and contraindication review
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Review pregnancy goals, relevant contraindications, and monitoring before use.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Isotretinoin without pregnancy prevention steps when applicable
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Major teratogenic risk; follow current prescribing safeguards.

teachingPearl: Treat nonpurulent cellulitis according to severity and local guidance; reassess promptly if it progresses or systemic toxicity develops.
traps: Missing a portal of entry or an abscess
Overlooking rapid progression, systemic toxicity, bullae, necrosis, or pain out of proportion
